acts: If cracks widen fast or you hear cracking: leave the building and move away from the edge
Call Civil Protection on 198, notify the municipality, return only when authorities allow
Photograph cracks with the date and mark their ends to track growth
Report any water or sewer leak: water is the main trigger of sliding
Do not add floors or dig foundations without a geotechnical study and a permit
assume: Simplified Bishop method, circular slip surfaces, 30 slices, automatic grid search of centres with two refinements
Hydrostatic pore pressure below the water table (no seepage); the entered unit weight applies above and below it
Pseudo-static earthquake (horizontal force kh·W toward the sea)
Idealised 2D section: does not model faults, non-circular failures or sea erosion
Check: ACADS example 1(a) gives 0.985 against a reference of ≈ 0.99
callD: Call immediately if new cracks appear, cracks widen quickly, or you hear cracking sounds.
causes: Rock type: fragile clay and sand layers with many faults and fractures
Rain and pipe leaks make the soil heavier and raise pore water pressure, which reduces friction
Sea erosion undercuts the foot of the cliff
Dense building and excavation add load and weaken the ground
circ: Critical circle: centre ({x}, {y}) m, radius {r} m, from x={a} to x={b} m.
errLay: Layer bases must decrease from top to bottom, and the last base must be ≤ 0.
errVal: Check the values: all fields are required and must be within reasonable limits.
iZw: Water table under the plateau (m above toe)
inspR: α = {a}° · W = {w} kN/m · u = {u} kPa · c′ = {c} kPa · φ′ = {p}° — black arrow: weight W, orange: seismic force kh·W, green: base resistance.
layNote: Base = elevation of the layer bottom relative to the toe. The last layer's base limits circle depth.
no3d: 3D is not available on this device or network. The 2D section is still available in the engineering tab.
none: No valid slip circle found with these inputs.
s3note: The scene is built from the engineering tool inputs: layers, water table, buildings and the critical slip circle. Drag to rotate, use + and − to zoom.
sensNote: Static factor of safety at different water levels, other inputs unchanged.
signs: New cracks in walls, floors or the road, or old cracks that widen
Doors and windows that suddenly stick
Walls, poles, trees or fences that tilt
Unusual water seepage or broken water or sewer pipes
Ground bulging or sinking, pavements pulling away from buildings
Cracking sounds or stones and soil falling from the cliff
src: Sources: La Presse, WMC, Kapitalis, Ultra Tunisia, Jawhara FM — last checked 16 September 2026. Follow official statements from the Ministry of Equipment and the municipality.
stFail: Rotational slide about the critical circle centre
stIdle: Ready — change the inputs or start the storm
stOk: The slope stays stable up to near-full saturation with these inputs
stRain: Heavy rain: the water table rises and the factor of safety drops
sub: Two parts: a residents' guide to warning signs and what to do, and a preliminary calculation tool for engineers using the simplified Bishop method.
target: Common reference values in practice: 1.5 for long-term static and 1.1 for seismic. Check the applicable standard (e.g. Eurocode 7).
title: Sidi Bou Said hill — awareness and preliminary geotechnical analysis
tl: Heavy rain, temporary evacuation of eight buildings and precautionary road closures
Head of Government decision no. 11 assigns the Ministry of Equipment to oversee studies and works
Agreements with the National Remote Sensing Centre (topography) and the National Office of Mines (geological and geophysical maps)
Phase 1 (diagnosis) results presented, works scheduled to start in August 2026
Press reports point to delays in the works as winter approaches
warnEng: Preliminary aid for engineers only. Results are indicative, are not an official assessment of any building or site, and do not replace the ongoing site investigation. Default values are examples: replace them with your borehole and lab results.
zwNote: Horizontal water table under the plateau, dropping linearly to sea level at the toe. Use a negative value for dry soil.
